subject: NorthBay expected run-rate + surge QPS — follow-up and numbers
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@northbayhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Quick follow-up on volumes & budget — NorthBay call recap

Marissa, thanks for the call earlier — helpful framing. I promised a short note with the signals our product/SRE team surfaced so you have the ground-truth for pricing. High level: we expect to run the clinical assistant and patient messaging features initially. A couple of quick clarifications so we can move toward a proposed hosted commit: 

- Expected monthly token footprint (initial 3–6 months): our internal estimate is 140M–200M tokens/month (conservative to aggressive).
- Peak observed TPS from our canary tests (15-minute windows): 40–95 TPS depending on batch timing; median peak ~60 TPS.
- Traffic shape: two daily spikes (09:00 and 20:00 PT) and occasional weekly surges after product pushes.
- Split: ~85% generation (chat) tokens, ~15% short embeddings for intent routing.

Budget: leadership gave a preliminary budget band of $8k–$20k/month for hosted LLM costs in the pilot phase (we can provide a $/1M target once you give unit assumptions).

Next steps for us: can you send a short hosted-API draft with committed baseline options and a 'surge' handling approach (burst or autoscale + cost sensitivity)? Attaching our SRE summary for visibility.

—Alex
NorthBay Product

Attachment: northbay-sre-traffic-patterns.pdf (summary, 2 pages)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@northbayhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 09:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up on volumes & budget — NorthBay call recap

Alex — thanks for the SRE notes, good context. Below is a concise capture of what we heard and an initial hosted pricing sketch so your finance/ops folks can run the numbers. If anything below is off, flag it and we’ll update the draft proposal.

Recap (from our call + SRE doc):
- Monthly token footprint (pilot / months 1–6): 140M–200M tokens/month. We’ll use 170M as a working median for math.
- Peak sustained TPS (short windows during launch events): 60–95 TPS. For SLA planning we recommend designing to 95 TPS peak with autoscale headroom.
- Workload mix: ~85% generation, ~15% embeddings; average generation request = 220 tokens in / 340 tokens out (signed off by product). Embeddings are small (~20 tokens).

Hosted pricing sketch (committed baseline + surge handling):
- Baseline commit: 150M tokens/month at a target rate of $11.00 per 1M tokens (hosted API committed tier). That yields ~ $1,650/month pre-discounts for month-to-month planning.
- Overages: billed at $13.50 per 1M tokens for any usage above the committed baseline within the billing month.
- Surge guardrails: automatic burst routing to a limited burst pool for short spikes (free up to 2x baseline TPS for up to 10 minutes/day); longer surges fall back to overage pricing.
- Optional reserved/dedicated conversation: if NorthBay wants predictable peak SLAs, we can map to a Dedicated pool — pricing would change (we can run that scenario if you expect > 250M tokens and sustained > 100 TPS).

Unit math (working example using 170M median):
- Committed baseline assumed: 150M @ $11/1M = $1,650/mo + overage for the extra 20M @ $13.50/1M = $270 => total ~ $1,920/mo.
- If you wanted a flat target budget of $10k/mo, that supports ~ 700M tokens at $11/1M (clearly larger than the pilot); helps to know midpoint budget targets.

Attachments I’m sending: pricing workbook with scenarios and a short proposal draft for NorthBay (redwood-proposal-northbay-draft.pdf, northbay_pricing_workbook.xlsx).

Ask: please confirm the monthly band you want us to price to (conservative 140M, working median 170M, aggressive 200M) and whether NorthBay prefers a firm committed baseline or a looser month-to-month committed band. Once you confirm, we’ll issue a one-page agreement draft + cost table and propose a POC timeline.

Thanks — Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: redwood-proposal-northbay-draft.pdf, northbay_pricing_workbook.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@northbayhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 11:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up on volumes & budget — NorthBay call recap

Alex — quick question from infra/ops: when you report the 40–95 TPS spikes, is that measured at the application ingress (pre-batching) or measured post-batch on our side? Small differences in the measurement change our concurrency plan and the recommended bucket sizes.

Also can you confirm whether the 85/15 generation/embedding split is expected to hold during surges (or do embeddings spike independently)? If embeddings spike more during certain flows we’ll recommend a slightly larger baseline to avoid embedding throttling.

If easier, Neha and I can hop on a 20-minute call with your SRE next week to correlate metrics.

—Karthik
Solutions

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@northbayhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up on volumes & budget — NorthBay call recap

Thanks — all that looks reasonable. Answers below and attaching a short internal note.

- TPS measurement: those numbers are at application ingress (pre-batching). Our telemetry currently aggregates per minute, but SRE extracted the 15-minute windows to show the short spikes.
- Generation/embedding split: we expect generation to remain ~80–87% even in surges; embeddings are fairly stable.
- Budget stance: leadership prefers a simple committed baseline for the pilot; they authorized pricing up to ~$12/1M for a 150M baseline with prompt to expand if we see steady growth. So your $11/1M baseline is in scope; if you can firm $11–12/1M in the proposal that will be easier to approve.

Next steps: we reviewed the workbook and like the two-tier commit + surge model. Please send a one-page agreement and an estimated POC runbook (2–4 weeks) by EOD Wednesday so we can nominate internal reviewers.

—Alex
Attaching: northbay-internal-approval-note.pdf
